title: Effective fppf descent for finite locally free covers of fixed degree
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $d\geq0$ be an integer. For each $S$-scheme $T$, let $\mathcal C_d(T)$ be the groupoid of schemes $Z$ with a finite locally free morphism $Z\to T$ of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free], whose arrows are $T$-isomorphisms. Pullback by scheme fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] preserves these objects and arrows. For every fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ [def-pc-fppf-site], suppose $Z_i\to T_i$ belong to $\mathcal C_d(T_i)$ and there are isomorphisms $\theta_{ij}:Z_i\times_TT_j\xrightarrow{\sim}T_i\times_TZ_j$ over $T_i\times_TT_j$ satisfying $\theta_{jk}\circ\theta_{ij}=\theta_{ik}$ on triple overlaps. There exist $Z\to T$ in $\mathcal C_d(T)$ and isomorphisms $Z\times_TT_i\simeq Z_i$ inducing the $\theta_{ij}$. For any two objects of $\mathcal C_d(T)$, compatible isomorphisms between their pullbacks to all $T_i$ descend to a unique $T$-isomorphism. Thus $\mathcal C_d$ is an fppf stack.

proof.text: For $f:Z\to T$ of degree $d$ and $g:T\prime\to T$, its pullback is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence], [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Its rank at $t\prime$ is the rank of $f$ at $g(t\prime)$ by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-rank-iso], hence is $d$. Thus it belongs to $\mathcal C_d(T\prime)$ by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] pulls back an isomorphism and its inverse. Identify both iterated pullbacks with the fibre product having the same $Z$ coordinate and ordered base coordinates; comparison maps preserve these coordinates. Their composites therefore agree by uniqueness, proving the pullback identity and composition coherences.

source.place: Tag 02VO, base-change direction; morphisms.tex Tags 02KD (lemma-base-change-finite-locally-free), 01WL, 01U9, 01TS; rank compatibility

proof.text: Given the datum in the statement, each $Z_i\to T_i$ is finite by [def-pc-finite-locally-free], hence affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Apply [lem-trf-fppf-family-coproduct-descent-encoding]: it constructs $A=\coprod_iT_i$, $V=\coprod_iZ_i$, an fpqc singleton $A\to T$, and the associated singleton descent datum on $V\to A$; its effectiveness is equivalent, for the same realizing scheme, to effectiveness of the original family datum. The map $V\to A$ is affine. Indeed choose affine open covers of each $T_i$; [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] gives an affine open cover of $A$ by their images. The inverse image of such an open in $V$ is its inverse image in the matching $Z_i$, since the other summands are disjoint. This is affine by affineness of $Z_i\to T_i$. The cover criterion [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] now proves the claim. This also handles infinite index sets.

Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-affine-descent-effective] to the singleton $A\to T$ and the affine morphism $V\to A$ of Step 2. It gives a scheme $Z\to T$ and an isomorphism $Z\times_TA\simeq V$ respecting the given singleton datum. The fixed-realization equivalence of [lem-trf-fppf-family-coproduct-descent-encoding] restricts this to isomorphisms $Z\times_TT_i\simeq Z_i$ inducing precisely the prescribed $\theta_{ij}$. At this point $Z$ is a scheme with the required descent identifications; its finiteness and degree are established next.

The original fppf family is fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. Under the isomorphisms of Step 3, all pullbacks of $Z\to T$ are finite, flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-finite], [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-flat], and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-locally-finite-presentation] separately to this same morphism and covering. Their conclusions give exactly finite local freeness of $Z\to T$. No quasi-compactness assumption on $T$ or on the coproduct covering map is used.

source.place: Tag 02VO (lemma-descending-property-finite-locally-free), proof citing Tags 02LA, 02L2 and 02KY; topologies.tex Tag 022C

proof.text: For any $t\in T$, joint surjectivity in [def-pc-fppf-site] supplies $i$ and $t_i\in T_i$ above $t$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-rank-iso] to the finite locally free map of Step 4. Its rank at $t$ equals the rank of its pullback at $t_i$, which is $d$ by the isomorphism with $Z_i$ and [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Rank is unchanged by this isomorphism: it identifies the fibre coordinate algebras linearly over $\kappa(t_i)$. Hence $Z\to T$ has degree $d$, giving effectivity in $\mathcal C_d$.

source.place: Tag 02VO, proof, final sentence: the degree is read off on fibres

proof.text: Let $Z,W$ be two global objects and let $b_i:Z\times_TT_i\simeq W\times_TT_i$ be compatible isomorphisms. The family $Z\times_TT_i\to Z$ is fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc] and [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. Compose $b_i$ with projection to $W$. Compatibility says these morphisms agree on every pairwise overlap, identified with $Z\times_TT_i\times_TT_j$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] gives a unique scheme map $b:Z\to W$. Its composite to $T$ equals the structure map of $Z$: they agree after this cover, so uniqueness in the same lemma with target $T$ proves equality. Thus $b$ is over $T$. Its pullback is $b_i$, since projections to $W$ and $T_i$ agree and fibre-product uniqueness applies.

The inverses $b_i^{-1}$ are compatible: invert the overlap commutation equations. Repeating Step 6 with $W,Z$ in place of $Z,W$ gives a $T$-map $c:W\to Z$. The maps $cb$ and $bc$ pull back to the identity on the respective fpqc covers. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] makes $cb=1_Z$ and $bc=1_W$. Hence $b$ is the unique descended $T$-isomorphism. Together with Steps 1--5 this proves the stack assertion. For an empty covering, joint surjectivity forces $T$ empty; every scheme mapping to it is empty, so effectiveness and uniqueness still hold. Degree zero and empty covering members cause no exception: the rank equalities and all the cited descent results include zero and require no positive degree.

lean.statement: theorem finiteLocallyFree_fppf_descent (S : Scheme.{u}) (T : Over S) (d : ℕ) : (∀ (Z : Over T.left), Z.hom.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree d → ∀ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : T' ⟶ T.left), (pullback.snd Z.hom g).IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree d) ∧ (∀ (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ T.left), Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage T.left → (∀ (D : SchemeCoverDescentDatum f), (∀ i, (D.localScheme i).hom.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree d) → ∃ (Z : Over T.left) (q : ∀ i, (D.localScheme i).left ⟶ Z.left), Z.hom.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree d ∧ (∀ i, IsPullback (q i) (D.localScheme i).hom Z.hom (f i)) ∧ ∀ (B : Scheme.{u}) (p : B ⟶ T.left) (i j : I) (a : B ⟶ U i) (b : B ⟶ U j) (ha : a ≫ f i = p) (hb : b ≫ f j = p) (x : (D.data.obj i).obj.obj (op ((Over.map a).obj (Over.mk (𝟙 B))))), ((D.representation j).homEquiv.symm ((D.data.hom p a b ha hb).hom.app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 B))) x)).left ≫ q j = ((D.representation i).homEquiv.symm x).left ≫ q i) ∧ (∀ (Z W : Over T.left), Z.hom.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree d → W.hom.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree d → ∀ (e : ∀ i, (Over.pullback (f i)).obj Z ≅ (Over.pullback (f i)).obj W), (∀ i j, pullback.fst (pullback.fst Z.hom (f i)) (pullback.fst Z.hom (f j)) ≫ (e i).hom.left ≫ pullback.fst W.hom (f i) = pullback.snd (pullback.fst Z.hom (f i)) (pullback.fst Z.hom (f j)) ≫ (e j).hom.left ≫ pullback.fst W.hom (f j)) → ∃! b : Z ≅ W, ∀ i, (Over.pullback (f i)).mapIso b = e i))
